title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own text. It is page 42 of a typed English preprint, and it was evidently filed in this cote among unrelated material. The neighbouring pages are handwritten French notes on exterior algebras and 'Algèbres de Hodge'.

The content is flat (fppf-type) cohomology of finite or affine group schemes ('AGS') over a local field k. By style and references it is very likely from Stephen S. Shatz's work on the cohomological dimension of Grothendieck topologies (mid-1960s). The citations fit that reading: [26] for a duality theorem, Tate [27], Berkson [5], Rosenberg–Zelinsky [21].

The page finishes one proof and states one new proposition.

(1) Conclusion of a theorem: H^r(A,G)=0 for r>2, where A is presumably a finite (artinian) k-algebra or similar and G a group scheme.
- Duality for AGS over a local field gives H^r(k,G')=0 for r>2.
- Prop. 14 (presumably a Leray / Hochschild–Serre type comparison between A and k that costs one degree) then gives vanishing for r>3.
- For r=3, Th. 1 reduces to A=k. Th. 4 together with duality gives H^3(k,G)≅H^3(k,G_s), where G_s is presumably a smooth or étale part of G.
- H^3(k,G_s) vanishes by Tate's results on Galois cohomology of local fields.

(2) Setup for the multiplicative group G_m. Take K/k purely inseparable. The face maps ⊗^r K → ⊗^{r+1} K induce maps H^s(⊗^r K, G_m) → H^s(⊗^{r+1} K, G_m). Their alternating sums form an Amitsur-type complex C(s).
- Prop. 15 states that C(s) is acyclic for every s>0.
- This is the input needed so that the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence collapses for the cover Spec K → Spec k. Flat cohomology of G_m over k is then computed by Amitsur cohomology of K/k, in the spirit of Rosenberg–Zelinsky and Berkson's work on Amitsur cohomology for purely inseparable extensions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page; the argument depends on Prop. 14, Th. 1, Th. 4 and Th. 6, which are not shown.
The page is misfiled: it is a typed English preprint by another author (probably S. S. Shatz), not Grothendieck's notes on Poincaré–Hodge algebras.

ideas.what: Vanishing of flat cohomology H^r(A,G) for r>2 for group schemes over a local field, via Tate-type duality plus a reduction step
ideas.modern_name: fppf cohomological dimension of local fields / flat duality for finite group schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shatz (1964–66), building on Tate; later Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems
ideas.where_published: Shatz, Annals papers on cohomology of artinian group schemes and the cohomological dimension of Grothendieck topologies (attribution likely but unconfirmed)

ideas.what: Acyclicity of the complex H^s(⊗^r K, G_m) for K/k purely inseparable, s>0
ideas.modern_name: Amitsur/Čech complex for purely inseparable extensions; collapse of the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shatz; related to Berkson and Rosenberg–Zelinsky on Amitsur cohomology

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of someone else's published-style preprint (likely Shatz) on flat cohomology, misfiled among Grothendieck's notes on standard conjectures. It contains no Grothendieck content and nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The wavy-underlined 'G_m' denotes the group scheme 𝔾_m (bold G_m); the transcription renders it correctly as \mathbb{G}_m.
'G_s' in H^3(k,G_s) is correct as transcribed (subscript s).
